case_title.reason: Case title matches the judgment heading.

number_of_accused.reason: Single appellant, Main Pal, is the only accused.

accused_religion.reason: Religion of the accused is not mentioned.

accused_caste.reason: Caste of the accused is not mentioned.

accused_occupation.reason: Occupation of the accused is not mentioned.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: No socioeconomic status of the accused is stated.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No prior criminal record is mentioned.

victim_gender.reason: Victims are women: Prakashi Devi (PW-1) and Sheela Devi.

victim_age.reason: No victim age is given in the judgment.

accused_victim_relationship.reason: Families were not on visiting terms and the accused had never entered the house, supporting 'stranger'.

offence_category.correct_value: Offences against women: criminal trespass and assault to outrage modesty
offence_category.quote: trespassing into the house of PW1 and attempting to outrage her modesty
offence_category.reason: Offences are trespass and outraging modesty; 'Cruelty' is not supported by the judgment.

statutory_provisions.reason: IPC ss. 452, 354 and CrPC ss. 211, 212, 215, 464 are all cited.

weapon.reason: No weapon is mentioned in the judgment.

evidence_type.correct_value: Eyewitness (oral testimony of PW-1 and PW-2)
evidence_type.quote: Her daughter-in-law Sheela Devi gave evidence as PW-2
evidence_type.reason: Eyewitness testimony is supported, but no circumstantial evidence is discussed.

confession.reason: No confession by the accused is mentioned.

trial_court_outcome.reason: Magistrate convicted under ss. 452 and 354 IPC and sentenced to six months RI.

high_court_outcome.correct_value: Conviction upheld; sentence reduced from six to four months rigorous imprisonment
high_court_outcome.quote: upholding the conviction but reducing the sentence from six to four months rigorous imprisonment
high_court_outcome.reason: High Court did not say 'Not applicable'; it upheld the conviction and reduced the sentence.

final_outcome.correct_value: Conviction set aside; matter remitted for a new trial
final_outcome.quote: The conviction of the accused-appellant is set aside and the matter is remitted to the trial court with a direction for a new trial
final_outcome.reason: Not an acquittal; the conviction was set aside and a new trial ordered.

offence_finally_established.reason: Since the conviction was set aside, no offence was finally established.

imprisonment_type.reason: No sentence survives the set-aside, so no final imprisonment type applies.

imprisonment_years.reason: No final sentence stands after the conviction was set aside.

fine_rs.reason: Trial fine of Rs.1,000 was not part of any surviving sentence, so null fits the final outcome.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Accused charged with trespass and assault to outrage modesty of PW-1; evidence showed assault on daughter-in-law; trial court convicted; High Court upheld conviction; facts stated without the Supreme Court's holding or remedy.
neutral_facts.quote: The Court concluded that the accused was prejudiced by the error in the charge and directed a new trial after framing a charge against the daughter-in-law.
neutral_facts.reason: Summary reveals the Supreme Court's holding and new-trial direction, which neutral facts must not disclose.

offence_severity.quote: convicted and sentenced him to rigorous imprisonment for six months
offence_severity.reason: Statutory minimum and maximum (six months to one year) do not appear in the judgment.

attempt_completion.reason: Charge describes an attempt to outrage modesty and an attempted trespass.

physical_harm.reason: Judgment does not address injuries; it only mentions the accused touching or catching the hand.

number_of_offences.reason: Two offences were charged and the High Court upheld both convictions.

financial_property_loss.quote: broke the bulbs and ran away
financial_property_loss.reason: Broken bulbs are mentioned, but no loss is valued, so 'Not applicable' is not the right label.

premeditation_planning.correct_value: Not found; the charge alleges 'after having made preparation for causing hurt or assault' with no finding
premeditation_planning.quote: after having made preparation for causing hurt or assault
premeditation_planning.reason: The charge alleges preparation, so 'Not stated' overlooks it, though no court finding exists.

motive.correct_value: Defence witness says a prior quarrel with complainant's son over a water course; no finding
motive.quote: there was a quarrel between the accused and complainant's son Surinder about a water course
motive.reason: A motive is asserted by the defence witness, so 'Not identified' is incomplete.

key_evidence_accepted.correct_value: Evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 showed the accused caught PW-1's daughter-in-law's hand and fled; the court held he was not charged with that offence
key_evidence_accepted.quote: he was not charged with such an offence
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Evidence is correctly described, but the court did not 'accept' a tried offence; it held he was never charged with it.

witness_credibility.correct_value: PW-1 and PW-2 said accused did not touch or abuse PW-1 but caught the daughter-in-law's hand; no explicit credibility finding
witness_credibility.quote: The evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 was that the appellant did not touch or tease or abuse Prakashi Devi.
witness_credibility.reason: Evidence is accurately described, but the court made no explicit credibility assessment.

post_offence_conduct.correct_value: Accused ran away after the victim raised an alarm
post_offence_conduct.quote: when she identified the accused and raised an alarm the accused ran away
post_offence_conduct.reason: The judgment states the accused fled when the alarm was raised; 'Not stated' is wrong.

trial_duration.correct_value: FIR registered 23.3.1996; trial judgment 2.2.2001; High Court order 16.3.2010; Supreme Court decision 7.9.2010
trial_duration.reason: Dates are right, but 23.3.1996 is the FIR date, not the start of trial.

legal_representation.reason: Appellant's counsel are named; no State counsel is listed.

investigation_status.reason: FIR, police report under s.173 and completed trial are supported.

procedural_irregularity.correct_value: Material error in the charge naming PW-1 instead of the daughter-in-law, violating s.212 CrPC
procedural_irregularity.quote: There was a material error in the charge as it violated the requirement of sub-section (1) of section 212 of the Code
procedural_irregularity.reason: The judgment identifies a material charge error, so 'None noted' is contradicted.

appeal_history.reason: Trial sentence, High Court reduction and Supreme Court outcome are all accurately reported.

prosecution_argument.correct_value: No separate prosecution argument stated; the appellate court and High Court held an accused cannot take advantage of a technical defect
prosecution_argument.quote: holding that an accused cannot take advantage of a technical defect in framing the charge
prosecution_argument.reason: The position attributed to the prosecution is the appellate and High Court's reasoning, not a stated prosecution argument.

defence_argument.reason: Defence argued the accused was not required to defend the Sheela Devi charge and should be acquitted.

legal_principle_applied.reason: Principles on fair play, ss. 211, 212, 215, 464 and the right to know the charge are accurately summarized.

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Willie (William) Slaney v. State of Madhya Pradesh AIR 1956 SC 116
